- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model frequently undercorrects; increase forecast slightly to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average, especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price increases (last 7–10 days); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.33), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before final prediction.
